strategy.summary: PR #2775 (linked issue #2581) fixes a non-terminating GCD bug in the Zippel farq/MPoly GCD path. In gcds_zippel, the LINZIP scale system for the reproducer inputs was generically underdetermined; the old code simply chose another evaluation point and kept retrying forever instead of escalating the number of images. All six added regression blocks (nmod_mpoly and fq_nmod_mpoly) hang on the buggy commit. The reproducing test to run is the first issue-2581 block in src/nmod_mpoly/test/t-gcd_zippel.c (equivalently src/fq_nmod_mpoly/test/t-gcd_zippel.c).

input_output_examples.input: nmod_mpoly_ctx_init(ctx, 12, ORD_LEX, 2147483647); vars = l1,l2,l3,a1,a2,a3,b1,b2,b3,g1,g2,g3; t = l1*a2-l1*a3-l2*a1+l2*a3+l3*a1-l3*a2; a = (b1*g2*g3+b2*g1*g3+b3*g1*g2)^2 then a = a*t*t; b = exact 30-term auxiliary polynomial (set in t-gcd_hensel.c issue-2581 block and copied verbatim into t-gcd.c/t-gcd_cofactors.c) then b = b*t; gcd_check(g, a, b, t, ctx, ...), expected gcd t.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: No gcd value is returned: repeated scalar-system failures send the caller to a new evaluation point indefinitely, so nmod_mpoly gcd test hangs and is killed by the CI 12 s timeout.
input_output_examples.expected_output: g == t; gcd_check passes, and the test completes in 0.2-1.1 s.

input_output_examples.input: fq_nmod_mpoly_ctx_init_deg(ctx, 12, ORD_LEX, UWORD(2147483647), 1); t = exact 12-variable polynomial from fq_nmod issue-2581 assertion (set in src/fq_nmod_mpoly/test/t-gcd_zippel.c); a = x3*(x5-x4)*t; b = x2*(x4-x6)*t; gcd_check(g, a, b, t, ctx,...), expected gcd t.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: fq_nmod_mpoly_gcd_zippel follows the same underdetermined-scale-system path and never terminates; the test hangs and is killed by the CI time limit.
input_output_examples.expected_output: g == t; the regression test passes and finishes in normal test time.

strategy.summary: Numerical accuracy bug (issue #2709): at buggy commit 50812d3 the acb_dft_rad2 plan builds its root-of-unity table by powering a call-precision root, so rounding error grows with root index and returned radii are about 2490x too wide at n=2^16, prec=128. PR #2756 adds regression test acb_dft_accuracy (t-accuracy.c) comparing plans built at prec vs prec+64 while running transforms at prec; on buggy code the radius ratio exceeds RATIO_MAX=8.0, so make check MOD=acb_dft fails. Reproduction will add/run only the PR test files, build the library, and observe the expected failure.

input_output_examples.input: acb_dft_rad2: n=2^16, working precision prec=128, exact integer input vector with zero input radius (pattern real=(i mod 19)-9, imag=(i mod 13)-6)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Plan root table built at call precision; output max radius about 2490x (~11 bits) too wide relative to achievable, with the looseness growing roughly linearly in n
input_output_examples.expected_output: Base root computed at prec+guard (prec + 6 + 2*FLINT_BIT_COUNT(len1)) and rounded back to prec; stored roots prec-accurate and output radius close to achievable (~1.5x for rad2)

input_output_examples.input: t-accuracy.c regression: n=2^8..2^14, prec=128, exact integer vector; acb_dft_rad2_precomp run at prec with plan initialized at prec and at prec+64; assert rlo/rhi <= RATIO_MAX=8.0 and growth <= GROWTH_MAX=4.0
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Radius ratio rlo/rhi about 10.5 at the first size and growing to about 54x over 2^8..2^14, so test prints FAIL (looseness): rad2 plan prec vs prec+64 ... ratio > 8 and aborts
input_output_examples.expected_output: Radius ratio about 1.5x for rad2 and 2-4x for bluestein, growth about 1x, so acb_dft_accuracy passes with ratio under 8.0 and growth under 4.0

strategy.summary: Reproduce issue #2421 / PR #2422 by building FLINT at the buggy revision and running the acb_poly_find_roots regression test added in src/acb_poly/test/t-find_roots.c. The test constructs the degree-4 geometric-progression polynomial with coefficients [10, -170, 2890, -49130, 835210], divides it by 83521 with 64-bit precision, and calls acb_poly_find_roots(roots, f, NULL, 40, 64). At this revision the initial-value selection can duplicate a starting point, so the solver does not return 4 roots and the regression test aborts with 'FAIL: geometric example'.

input_output_examples.input: acb_poly_t f; acb_poly_set_coeff_si(f, 0, 10); acb_poly_set_coeff_si(f, 1, -170); acb_poly_set_coeff_si(f, 2, 2890); acb_poly_set_coeff_si(f, 3, -49130); acb_poly_set_coeff_si(f, 4, 835210); acb_set_ui(c, 83521); acb_poly_scalar_div(f, f, c, 64); roots = _acb_vec_init(4); acb_poly_find_roots(roots, f, NULL, 40, 64)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: return value != 4, so the new test block triggers 'FAIL: geometric example' and flint_abort(). The exact wrong root count is not printed in the test; issue #2421 reports an incomplete result for this geometric-progression class (fewer than four roots isolated).
input_output_examples.expected_output: acb_poly_find_roots returns 4, i.e. all four roots are isolated and the new regression block completes without aborting.

strategy.summary: Issue #2329 / PR #2330: arb_get_interval_arf and arb_get_interval_mpfr compute the interval endpoints as mid +/- radius. When a ball has a non-NaN midpoint and an infinite radius, e.g. midpoint=-Inf and radius=+Inf, the old code computes -Inf + Inf for the upper endpoint and returns NaN. The PR fixes source so infinite-radius/non-NaN-midpoint balls return the full extended interval (-Inf,+Inf), and strengthens the two interval tests to reject NaN endpoints in this case. Reproduce by building the buggy commit with the PR's test-only assertions applied, then run the two interval tests and observe the FAIL/abort.

input_output_examples.input: x = setball(Arb, -Inf, Inf), so arb_midref(x) = -Inf and arb_radref(x) = +Inf; queried via arb_get_interval_arf (or arb_get_interval_mpfr); old endpoint computation forms -Inf + Inf for the upper endpoint.
input_output_examples.expected_output: interval endpoints are (-Inf, +Inf), with no NaN endpoint

input_output_examples.input: Random x from arb_randtest satisfying mag_is_inf(arb_radref(x)) and !arf_is_nan(arb_midref(x)); endpoints a,b from arb_get_interval_arf, or aa,bb from arb_get_interval_mpfr; then y is the interval formed from those endpoints.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: At least one arf/mpfr endpoint is NaN, so the strengthened assertion (!arf_is_nan(arb_midref(x)) && (arf_is_nan(a) || arf_is_nan(b))) fails (NaN of the output interval endpoint).
input_output_examples.expected_output: Neither endpoint is NaN and arb_contains(y, x) holds.

strategy.summary: PR flintlib/flint#2322 fixes arb_div/arb_div_arf producing NaN/non-finite values when the midpoint of x is exactly zero at high precision (x = 0 or x = [0 +/- eps]). The PR adds two checks to src/arb/test/t-div.c at prec = 100000. At the buggy commit fbc8b902e4366dbf346d589f8327d4bd1f08ac8a these checks abort the test program, so reproduction consists of building the repo and running the FLINT test suite from that commit.

input_output_examples.input: x = 0 (arb_init(x), no radius set), y = 3^(-1) computed as arb_set_ui(y,3); arb_inv(y,y,100000); then arb_div(z, x, y, 100000)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: NaN (arb_is_zero(z) is false; test prints 'FAIL: 0 / y at high precision' and aborts)

input_output_examples.input: x = [0 +/- 1e-10] (arb_midref(x) = 0, mag_set_d(arb_radref(x), 1e-10)); y = approximately 1/3 with radius zeroed by mag_zero(arb_radref(y)); then arb_div(z, x, y, 100000)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: NaN / non-finite (arb_is_finite(z) is false; test prints 'FAIL: [0 +/- eps] / y at high precision' if reached)
input_output_examples.expected_output: Finite ball centered at 0, radius approximately 1e-10 / (1/3) = 3e-10, i.e. [0 +/- eps/|y|]; arb_is_finite(z) is true
